Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05

Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Verve - Head of ML), Derek Holt (CTO), Priya Singh (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick hosted API walkthrough focusing on chat/text generation basics. Demos streaming and param tuning. Some word recognition issues in transcription, please refer to shared deck link.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Samir from Redwood, I have Lena with me, yeah thanks for carving out time.
[00:12] Maya: Hi hi, thanks, we just hopped in, Derek's on our side too. Quick heads up, Priya from security will pepper in with SOC2 questions.
[00:20] Samir: Perfect, plan is 30 minutes demo, 5-10 for Q+A, we'll show Hosted API chat and then Console bits. Any must-see items before we start?
[00:30] Derek: We want to understand latency numbers and costs, also streaming behavior for UI.
[00:38] Lena: Great, we'll show streaming in the browser and also how parameters affect token usage, like temperature and top_p, and max_tokens.
[00:48] Samir: Also touch on retries, idempotency keys — common in production.
[00:52] Maya: Awesome. We have sample prompts and a small test harness, we'll share after.
[01:05] Lena: Alright, sharing my screen, open the quickstart. So Hosted API, basic chat endpoint, you can stream partial tokens, it's server-sent events, websockets or SSE depending on client. Note: transcription may show Redwood product name as Redwood infer, sometimes mis-typed in logs.
[01:28] Lena: Here's an example request: role user system messages, model param, temperature 0.2, top_p 0.95, max_tokens 256. If you lower temperature you'll get more deterministic outputs.
[01:45] Maya: So streaming means we can render tokens as they arrive, right? How about partial completions when connection drops?
[01:55] Lena: Yes, tokens stream incrementally. If connection drops you can resume with the same conversation state if you persisted the conversation id/k-v cache on your side — or re-request with the messages array, but it's more efficient to store the last turn.
[02:15] Derek: Any built-in resume mechanism?
[02:18] Lena: Not an automatic TCP resume; we recommend idempotency keys at the request layer and persisting the last messages. There's also server-side session tokens but for Hosted API we suggest client-managed conversation state for scale.
[02:35] Samir: Quick note on retries: use idempotency keys and exponential backoff. If you re-send without idempotency you might get duplicated tokens or different responses — models are nondeterministic.
[02:50] Priya: How do you guarantee audit logs for compliance? We need per-request metadata stored for x months.
[02:58] Samir: Redwood stores request/response metadata by default for debugging — retention is configurable (per plan). For Private and Dedicated customers you can push logs to your SIEM or self-host retention. We'll share the security docs.
[03:12] Priya: What about encryption keys? KMS?
[03:15] Lena: We integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments; hosted supports customer-managed keys in certain tiers. I'll share the KMS integration doc link.
[03:25] Maya: Back to streaming, what's the per-token latency you see on average?
[03:30] Lena: For small models on Hosted we typically see token latencies ~20-40ms on optimized instances, on larger models it's higher. Our public benchmarks show p50/p95 numbers, we'll attach that.
[03:45] Derek: That sounds optimistic — what hardware? GPUs?
[03:50] Lena: It's a mix — our hosted pool uses high-throughput inference instances, kernel selection changes based on sequence length. For fairness we'll share the model profile matrix in the deck.
[04:05] Lena: Now demo time: I'm hitting the chat endpoint with streaming param, you'll see tokens arriving.
[04:20] [screen share demo — partial audio: keyboard typing, short pause]
[04:30] Lena: Here you can see the SSE chunks come in, each chunk is a delta. Client stitches them. We also show how to set stop sequences to truncate.
[04:45] Maya: If we set stop sequences incorrectly could we end up with partial sentences?
[04:50] Lena: Yes, careful tuning matters. Stop sequences work as token-level patterns, so sometimes punctuation or whitespace mis-hits. That's why we recommend eval sets.
[05:05] Samir: Speaking of evals, Redwood Optimize helps detect regressions by running a prompt suite and surfacing quality changes tied to model/version changes.
[05:15] Maya: That looks useful, especially for finance phrasing.
[05:20] Derek: Cost controls — can you throttle or set per-route limits?
[05:25] Samir: Yes, Console has per-route quotas, rate limits, and token-based cost dashboards. You can also route lower priority traffic to cheaper model variants.
[05:40] Lena: Example: continuous batching reduces compute by combining small requests. Optimize recommends batching thresholds that balance latency and cost.
[05:55] Maya: On batching, do we need to change prompts or anything?
[06:00] Lena: No, batching is transparent to the client — it's server-side. But you might see slightly higher tail latency for very small requests because batch windows wait briefly.
[06:15] Derek: What's the typical tradeoff window?
[06:18] Lena: Typically 10-50ms batching delay for big throughput gains; you can tune the policy per-pool.
[06:30] Priya: For PII and PCI we need data residency in eu-west-1 and logs retention off-platform. Is that doable?
[06:38] Samir: Yes, region pinning and private options support that; Dedicated/Private deployments meet that requirement. For hosted we have region controls but retention is plan dependent.
[06:52] Priya: Are you SOC2 Type II audited?
[06:55] Samir: Yes, Redwood has SOC2; we also provide ISO docs on request. I'll attach the attestation.
[07:05] Maya: Any rate limits for streaming connections?
[07:08] Lena: There are connection limits per account and per-pool; typical customers don't hit them but we can provision.
[07:18] Maya: Ok great. Can you show retry pattern example code?
[07:22] Lena: Sure, here's a snippet: send request with idempotency_key header, if 5xx or network error then exponential backoff, break on 4xx. For streaming, if you lose connection mid-stream you can re-request the full last message and use the idempotency_key to avoid consuming tokens twice in billing.
[07:50] Derek: Billing question — are partial streamed tokens billed if a stream fails?
[07:56] Samir: Billing is per-token generated. If a stream breaks the tokens returned still count; if you re-request with the same idempotency key we detect duplication and avoid double billing in many cases — we'll send the exact billing semantics doc.
[08:15] Lena: Moving to Console — you get token-level charts, per-route latency, and error traces. You can also drill into a particular request and see the input/output.
[08:30] [screen share: console dashboard noise]
[08:40] Lena: Here is an A/B rollout example: you can direct 10% traffic to a new model, failover rules if latency breaches SLO, and automatic fallback to stable model.
[08:55] Maya: That auto-fallback is important for us. If a high-value flow degrades we need rollback.
[09:02] Samir: Exactly, that's built-in. Also safe deploys with canary and gradual increases.
[09:12] Derek: Any integrations with our telemetry stack?
[09:15] Samir: Yes, you can push traces to your tracing backend or set up webhooks for alerts. We'll share webhook spec.
[09:28] Priya: On the security side, can we get VPC peering or Private Link?
[09:33] Lena: For Dedicated we support VPC peering and PrivateLink; Private deployments support on-prem. For hosted we offer private endpoints in some regions.
[09:45] Maya: Let's talk about model variants — do you have quantized models to save cost?
[09:50] Lena: Yes, we have quantized variants and recommended quantization profiles; Optimize suggests which variant per workload. The tradeoff is small quality drop in some tasks.
[10:05] Derek: How do we test quality differences?
[10:08] Lena: Use Optimize's eval runner
upload prompts and reference outputs, it scores outputs across models and quantization settings. We'll share a sample eval template.
[10:22] Maya: Can we attach our custom safety filters?
[10:25] Samir: You can run post-processing filters on the client or use server-side hooks in Private deployments. For hosted, recommended pattern is client-side filtering with Console alerting.
[10:40] [short pause, background typing sounds]
[10:52] Lena: Now a quick live prompt: we ask the model to summarize a policy paragraph. Notice temperature 0.0 for deterministic summarization and stop sequence to end at newline.
[11:12] [model streaming tokens audible as pings in demo]
[11:22] Maya: Looks clean. How about long context handling? We have documents tens of thousands of tokens.
[11:28] Lena: For long contexts we do chunking and retrieval-augmented generation patterns; Redwood supports long context models and KV cache management for latents. For very long documents we recommend embeddings + RAG.
[11:45] Derek: Are embeddings separate billing?
[11:48] Samir: Yes embeddings billed per-unit; Console will show combined cost per flow.
[11:55] Priya: If we do POC, can we get sample legal terms for data usage?
[11:59] Samir: Yes we'll include the data processing addendum and security attachments.
[12:08] Maya: For POC scope, we want to test two flows: chat summarization and automated compliance Q&A. Latency target p95 < 500ms for chat and accuracy > 92 on our eval set within 2 weeks.
[12:24] Derek: And cost per 1k tokens target?
[12:27] Maya: We'd like to keep cost under $0.80 per 1k tokens for low-latency model if possible.
[12:35] Lena: We'll propose model variants to meet that — often hybrids: a smaller low-latency model for interactive flows and a larger backend for heavy reasoning.
[12:50] Samir: Ok, summary of POC: 2 flows, test harness, eval set, 2 week run. We'll propose infra and costs.
[13:02] [brief side chat about calendar invites and stakeholders]
[13:20] Priya: A few security specifics: can you redact logs automatically? We need PII masking before logs leave our VPC.
[13:30] Lena: For Private and Dedicated we can do pre-ingest masking; for hosted we provide redaction tooling but recommend client-side masking for the strictest control.
[13:45] Maya: Great. Any tricky gotchas you've seen in production on streaming?
[13:50] Lena: Biggest gotcha is retry semantics — if clients retry naively you can double charge or get duplicate replies. Use idempotency keys, and persist conversation state. Also watch stop sequences and tokenization mismatches causing truncation.
[14:05] Derek: Noted. Can you send sample retry code?
[14:08] Lena: Yes, included in the action items.
[14:15] Samir: Last section, pricing tiers quick callout: Pay-as-you-go for hosted, reserved capacity for Dedicated. We'll include the tier spreadsheet.
[14:28] Maya: Any discounts for committed usage?
[14:30] Samir: Yes, reserved commits for Dedicated and committed usage discounts for hosted via commitments — we can talk numbers in follow-up.
[14:40] [closing portion — 5 minute Q+A left]
[14:45] Priya: One more Q on data residency — log push to our S3 in eu-west-1, is that supported?
[14:50] Lena: Supported for Dedicated/Private; for hosted we have region-local retention but direct push requires Dedicated-type integration.
[15:05] Maya: Let's confirm timeline: we want POC by mid-March. Can you get us a proposal by Friday?
[15:12] Samir: We'll aim for Friday (2026-03-06). Lena will attach the benchmark and sample scripts.
[15:20] Derek: Thanks both, that was helpful.
[15:25] Samir: Thanks, we'll follow up with docs and next steps.
